entries.en_definition: The rate at which an object changes its velocity (i.e. speeds up, slows down or changes direction). Equation: a = Δv/Δt
entries.to_definition: Ko e vave 'o e liliu 'o e 'alu hake pe ko e hifo tuai pe fetongi hala fononga 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi a = Δv/Δt.

entries.en_definition: A type of radiation sent out by radioactive elements which consist of alpha (α) particles that are high speed nuclei of helium (⁴₂He²+)
entries.to_definition: Ko e fa'ahinga huelo 'oku tuku atu 'e he 'elemeniti mo'ui 'oku 'i ai e tekonga 'alifa 'oku vave fau hono uho'i 'atomi heliumi (⁴₂He²+).

entries.en_definition: This is "how high" a wave is or the maximum displacement of a wave from its rest /equilibrium position
entries.to_definition: Ko e ma'olunga 'o e peau mei he laine mālōlō.

entries.en_definition: The pressure exerted by the weight of air in the atmosphere of the earth (Pressure = Force/Area, i.e Pressure is Force per unit Area)
entries.to_definition: Ko e ta'au 'o e 'ea mei he 'atimosifia 'o e mamani 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi P = Force/Area

entries.en_definition: A force that is exerted between two objects that are in physical contact or touching each other (e.g. Applied force; pushing a box)
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi ta'omi mei he ongo me'a 'e 2 'oku na fefa'uhi fakasino.

entries.en_definition: This refers to the flow of electric charge from the positive terminal (+) of a power source/battery to the negative terminal (-).
entries.to_definition: Ko e fetafeaki 'a e ivi 'uhila mei he pou positivi ki he pou nekativi 'o e maka kasa.

entries.en_definition: This is when the speed of an object slows down & the acceleration becomes negative (e.g. a = - 15 m/s²)
entries.to_definition: Ko e holo e vave 'o e lele 'a ha me'a pea nekativi leva e liu vave.

entries.en_definition: This is mass per unit volume of a substance (Density = Mass/Volume) or the ratio of the mass of a substance to its volume.
entries.to_definition: Ko e fua mā'opo'opo 'o fakatatau ki he 'ekuasi ko e D=M/V pē ko e falakiseni 'o e mamafa ki hono voliume.

entries.en_definition: The current or electric charge that moves constantly in a one direction only (e.g. battery). Also known as DC current.
entries.to_definition: Ko e tafe 'a e ivi 'uhila tu'uma'u ki he feitu'u pē 'e taha hangē ko e maka kasa.

entries.en_definition: This is a device used to convert chemical energy into electrical energy (also known as an electrochemical cell).
entries.to_definition: Ko e me'angāue 'oku ne liliu e ivi kemikale ki he ivi'i 'uhila.

entries.en_definition: The rate at which charge flows pass a point in an electric circuit. Electric Current = I = Q/t where Q = quantity of charge, t = time
entries.to_definition: Ko e vave 'o e tafe 'ae ivi 'uhila 'i he fatakamilo 'uhila 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi I=Q/t.

entries.en_definition: The piece of metal used to connect the solution & the circuit in an electrochemical cell. E.g. Anodes (-) & Cathodes (+).
entries.to_definition: Ko e metali 'oku ne fakahoko 'a e solusoni ki he fakatakamilo 'uhila hangē ko e Anote (-) mo e Kefote (+).

entries.en_definition: Waves cause by oscillations of electric & magnetic field & are able to travel through a vacuum (e.g. light).
entries.to_definition: Kaupeau fakatupu 'e he femalele'aki 'a e ivi 'uhila mo e makineti pea 'oku lava 'o fakafononga he 'āngoa.

entries.en_definition: The non-contact electric force between charged particles. It can be attractive (e.g. + & - charges) or repulsive (+ & + or - & - charges).
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi 'uhila mei he naunau tekonga 'oku fetokanga'aki (positivi pe nekativi) pe fesītu'a'aki (positivi pe nekativi).

entries.en_definition: Any push or pull exerted on an object measured in Newtons (N)
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi fusi pe teke 'oku ta'omi ki ha me'a. 'Okou fua'aki e 'iuniti Niutoni (N).

entries.en_definition: The number of waves passing any point each second. Frequency (measured in Hz) = f = T/1 where T = Period (measured in seconds).
entries.to_definition: Ko e lahi 'o e peau kuo fakalaka 'i ha poini he sekoni 'e taha 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi F= T/1.

entries.en_definition: When two surfaces are in contact, there is a force that resists movement. This force is known as Friction.
entries.to_definition: I he taimi 'oku fetaulaki ai ha ongo tafa'aki 'e 2 pea 'oku 'i ai e malohi faka'apulu e ngāue.

entries.en_definition: A fuse contains a thin wire which melts if the electric current is too high (i.e. a small electrical safety device)
entries.to_definition: Ko e fiusi ko e ki'i uaea manifi 'oku vaia kapau 'oku fu'u mālohi e 'uhila tafe.

entries.en_definition: Reaction where two smaller nuclides combine into one larger nuclide & release energy
entries.to_definition: Ko e fakataha'i 'a e nukilaiti iiki 'e 2 ke ma'u ai e taha lahi mo e ivi.

entries.en_definition: High energy electromagnetic radiation so has no mass & no charge (i.e. is part of the electromagnetic spectrum)
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi ma'olunga 'uhilamakineti 'oku 'ikai hano mamafa, positivi pe nekativi.

entries.en_definition: This is another way of expressing the slope (i.e. how steep a straight line is). Gradient = rise/run
entries.to_definition: Ko e founga 'e taha hono fakamatala'i e tahakehake hangē ko e 'ekuasi G=rise/run.

entries.en_definition: The force of gravity (Fg) that exists between earth & the objects that are near it, causing objects to accelerate (i.e. g = 9.81 m/s²)
entries.to_definition: Ko e māloohi 'o e kalāvite he vaha'a 'o mamani mo e me'a ofi ki ai 'o fakatupu 'enau liu vave pea ta'eliliu mei he 9.81 m/s².

entries.en_definition: Time taken for half the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay
entries.to_definition: Ko e taimi 'oku 'aunga ai e vaeua 'o e huelo faka'atomi.

entries.en_definition: The change in momentum (Δp) produced by a force (F) acting for a length of time (t). Impulse = I = Δp = FΔt
entries.to_definition: Ko e liliu e takina fakatupu 'e he malohi 'oku ngāue ki he fa'ahinga taimi 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi I = Δp = FΔt.

entries.en_definition: Materials that do not allow the free flow of electrons or electrical current (e.g. plastic). Insulator is the opposite of a conductor.
entries.to_definition: Ko e matelia 'oku tapu ke ne fakafononga e 'ilekituloni pe 'uhila tafe hangē ko e pelesitiki.

entries.en_definition: Energy possessed by an object due to its motion. Kinetic Energy = Ek = ½ mv² where m = mass, v = velocity
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi ngāue 'o ha me'a hangē ko e 'ekuasi Ek = ½ mv².

entries.en_definition: The region around a magnet in which a magnetic force is exerted (i.e. where iron or other magnets experience a force)
entries.to_definition: Ko e 'elia fakamakineti mei he malohi 'o ha makineti.

entries.en_definition: The quantity of matter in an object. The unit of mass is kg or g (1kg is the mass of 1 liter of water at about 4°C).
entries.to_definition: Ko e kakano 'o e matelie: ko e 1kg 'oku tatau ia 'o e lita vai 'e 1 he 4°C.

entries.en_definition: The study of motion of objects & equilibrium. Kinematics (motion) & Dynamics (forces) are the two main branches of Mechanics.
entries.to_definition: Ko e saienisi 'o e me'a 'oku ngaue, nga'unu pea palanisi. 'Oku konga lalahi e 2 ko e Kinamatika mo e Tainamika

entries.en_definition: The product of the mass and velocity of a moving object or body. Momentum = p = mv
entries.to_definition: Ko e takina 'oku fika'i mei he kakano mo e vave 'o e ngaue 'a ha me'a 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi p = mv.

entries.en_definition: The Standard International (SI) unit of force. A force of one newton (1 N) will give an object of mass 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s².
entries.to_definition: Ko e 'iuniti Niutoni 'a e malohi 'o e teke pe fusi. Ko e niutoni 'e 1 te ne 'ave 'a e mamafa 1kg 'aki e vave ko e 1 m/s².

entries.en_definition: The energy released when the nuclei of large atoms split apart (i.e. fission reaction) or when smaller nuclei combine in fusion reactions.
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi faka'atami ne pu'aki mai 'e he uho'i 'atomi lalahi ne mavaeua.

entries.en_definition: The relationship between voltage (V), resistance (R) and current (I) is given by Ohm's Law: V=IR
entries.to_definition: Ko e lao 'a 'Oumi ko e vā 'o e volota, taliteke'i mo e 'uhila tafe.

entries.en_definition: The regular, repeating path that one object in space takes around another one due to the force of gravity (e.g.planets orbit the sun)
entries.to_definition: Ko e vilovilo tu'uma'u 'a e me'a 'i he 'atā 'o fakatatau ki he malohi 'o e kalāvite.

entries.en_definition: Power = P = W/t where W=Work, t=time. Power is the rate at which work is done.
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi malohinga 'o ha me'a ko e vave 'oku lava 'osi ki ai e ngāue 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi P=W/t

entries.en_definition: Pressure = P = F/A or force per area in N/m².
entries.to_definition: Ko e malohi 'oku ne ta'omi ha 'elia 'o hange ko e 'ekuasi P=F/A

entries.en_definition: Isotopes with unstable nuclei/parent nuclei which can spontaneously emit particles or radiation leaving new nuclei/daughter nuclei
entries.to_definition: Ko e 'isotope uho'i 'atomi ta'emanofo 'oku ne lava 'o pu'aki mai e tekonga 'atomi pe ivi'i 'atomi.

entries.en_definition: Reaction force exists at the same time as the Action force with equal magnitudes but they act in opposite directions (i.e. Newton's 3rd Law).
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi fakafoki 'o e ivi ngāue he taimi tatau, 'aki 'a e malohi tatau ka ko e feitu'u fehangahangai (Ko e Lao hono 3 ia 'a Niutoni)

entries.en_definition: The change in speed & direction when light or waves travels from one mediem to another (e.g. from air to water)
entries.to_definition: Ko e liliu 'o e vave mo e feitu'u he taimi 'oku fononga ai e maama pe peau mei he matelie 'e taha ki he taha.

entries.en_definition: It's how much an electrical component restricts the flow of current. The lower the resistance (R) the better the current flows.
entries.to_definition: Ko e taliteke'i 'o e 'uhila tafe.

entries.en_definition: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of the substance by 1 degree Celsius (e.g. water, c = 4180 J kg‾¹ °C‾¹)
entries.to_definition: Ko e māfana 'oku fiema'u ke fakamāfana'i e matelie 1kg 'aki e tikilī 'e taha.

entries.en_definition: It's how fast an object is travelling & it's a scalar quantity (i.e. direction is not important). Speed = v = d/t where d = distance, t = time
entries.to_definition: Ko e vave 'o e fakafononga 'o ha me'a hangē ko e 'ekuasi v=d/t. Ko e fononga ki ha fa'ahinga feituu pe (e.g. 5 m/s)

entries.en_definition: The pulling force in a rope/string when stretched under an external force (e.g. ball hanging on a string, tension force equals the weight force)
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi falō 'o ha maea he taimi 'oku falō ai 'e ha ivi fakatu'a.

entries.en_definition: Derived from the Greek word "therme" which means heat. Heat is used to denote thermal energy (which is really kinetic energy).
entries.to_definition: Ko e ivi māfana ko e ma'u mei he lea Kalisi.

entries.en_definition: Waves where the particles of the medium oscillate or vibrate at right angles or 90° to the direction the waves are travelling.
entries.to_definition: Ko e peau 'oku vilovilo hono tekonga 'atomi tikilī 'e 90 ki he feitu'u 'oku fononga ki ai e peau.

entries.en_definition: Uncertainty of a single measurement is given by the least count of the measuring instrument (e.g. 10.5 ± 0.1 mm if vernier calliper is used).
entries.to_definition: Oku veiveiua 'a e fua tu'otaha 'o ha me'a. 'Oku fakafuofua'i ia mei he fua si'isi'i taha 'o e me'angaue.

entries.en_definition: Refers to a space devoid of matter & is characterized by the absence of air & other gases (i.e. no particles, pressure = 0)
entries.to_definition: Ko e feitu'u 'oku hala'atā ha matelie 'i ai na'a mo e 'ea.

entries.en_definition: The speed in a given direction & it's a vector quantity measured in m/s. Velocity = v = d/t where d = displacement, t=time
entries.to_definition: Ko e vave 'o e fononga ki ha feitu'u pea mo hono taimi hangē ko e 'ekuasi v= d/t (e.g. 5 m/s North)

entries.en_definition: The distance between two successive corresponding positions in a wave (e.g. distance between two successive crests or troughs)
entries.to_definition: Ko e vaha'a kaupeau 'e 2 hokohoko 'oku fua mei he poini tatau.

entries.en_definition: The force (F) applied times the distance moved by the object in the direction of the force. Work = W = F×d where d=displacement
entries.to_definition: Ko e ngāue 'oku fika'i ia mei he lahi e malohi 'oku faka'aonga'i ke ue'i ha me'a ki he feitu'u tatau 'o hangē ko e 'ekuasi W=Fxd.
